sections.section_title: 1. Epidemiology & Pathophysiology of Capnocytophaga canimorsus Infection
sections.description: This section introduces the zoonotic source of the patient’s illness and explains why *C.* canimorsus poses a unique risk in human disease. It covers the bacterium’s biology, how it interacts with the host immune system—particularly the complement pathways—and why it can trigger a complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy in susceptible individuals.
subtopics: Dog-bite epidemiology and human exposure risk
Microbiology of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus*: Gram-negative rod morphology and encapsulation
Clinical spectrum ranging from localized cellulitis to fulminant sepsis
Overview of innate immunity with emphasis on the alternative complement pathway
Mechanisms by which *C.* canimorsus activates complement leading to endothelial injury
"Second hit" model—how infections trigger latent complement dysregulation
Genetic susceptibility in CM‑HUS : CFH/CFI/CFB variants or anti-factor H antibodies

sections.description: Here the reader learns the patient’s symptom chronology—from bite day through evolving septic shock—and details how early laboratory data suggested disseminated intravascular coagulation in the setting of severe bacteremia.
subtopics: "Day‑0" bite event through high fever development over four days
"Day‑4" presentation with hypoglycaemia prompting ED transfer
WBC pattern indicating profound leukocytopenia combined with neutrophilia
DIC evidence from prolonged PT/PTT, low fibrinogen, high d-dimer
Acute kidney injury markers at admission – increasing creatinine/BUN
Early imaging studies used to rule out necrotising fasciitis or vascular catastrophe
Broad-spectrum empirical therapy chosen based on dog-bite flora
